claims.text: The as-synthesized catalyst is an equimolar nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid solution.
The as-synthesized PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst has a random atomic distribution.
Mild thermal or oxidative pretreatment can increase the surface isolation of Pt/Pd sites without causing bulk phase segregation or sintering.
Ethanol oxidation behavior on nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs is governed by the degree of surface isolation of Pt/Pd active sites.
Neighboring oxophilic Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os atoms electronically modulate surface Pt/Pd sites.
The proposed pretreatment shifts the d-band centers of Pt/Pd sites.
The Pt/Pd electronic shift optimizes adsorption of ethanol oxidation intermediates.
The spatial and electronic modulation of Pt/Pd suppresses poisoning species during ethanol oxidation.
The pretreatment selectively oxidizes or otherwise modifies the more oxophilic Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os components.
Modified Rh, Ru, Ir, and Os reduce the binding strength of poisoning intermediates at nearby Pt/Pd atoms.
Alloying can create isolated Pt and Pd sites and charge transfer to those sites, enhancing adsorbate interaction and catalytic activity.
Spatial modulation prevents the formation of contiguous noble-metal surface ensembles.
Contiguous noble-metal ensembles favor overoxidation or catalyst poisoning during ethanol oxidation.
Pretreated catalysts will have a lower ethanol-oxidation onset potential than untreated catalysts.
Pretreated catalysts will exhibit higher ethanol-oxidation current density than untreated catalysts.
Pretreatment will shift the product distribution toward acetaldehyde or acetic acid and away from CO2.
The proposed mechanism applies only when pretreatment does not produce significant sintering or phase separation.
Extreme temperatures or potentials may generate different surface reconstructions outside the scope of the mechanism.
Surface-sensitive characterization can quantify Pt/Pd isolation and associated electronic changes.
